regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY looks like acceleration — until you note that IIP overall slowed to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%, core sector moderated to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%, and the PMI composite at 54.6 is services-led (54.5) while manufacturing slips to 52.8. The quality of growth is narrowing: capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is encouraging, but the divergence between the headline GDP print and the goods economy suggests the formal services sector is doing the heavy lifting while the broader economy moderates.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"The headline CPI at 4.45% YoY understates the problem: fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile print — is feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY, and the RBI has already revised its inflation forecast up to 5.1% YoY from 4.6%. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY is above the 4% target on its own, meaning this is not purely a food or fuel story. The inversion: if RBI holds at 5.25% p.a. while its own forecast sits at 5.1% YoY inflation, the real rate is barely positive — insufficient to anchor expectations if Brent sustains above $100/bbl.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY — a 630bps divergence — has pushed the CD ratio to 81.4% credit ÷ deposits, the 75th percentile historically. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% signals wholesale funding is being tapped to bridge the gap. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% with repo at similar levels was FY14; within 12 months the system faced a funding squeeze that forced emergency macro-prudential action. Industry credit at 20% YoY and services credit at 22.9% YoY are the concentrated pressure points.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is on extended pause, but the RBI's own inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY leaves the real rate at roughly 80bps — thin cover for an economy where fuel inflation is at a 10-year high and the CD ratio is flashing amber. The signal for housing: average home loan rates at 7.65% p.a. against an affordability index at a record-worst 10.9× price ÷ income means rate cuts, if they come, will arrive too late to rescue affordability. For FX management, INR at 95.24 ₹/USD (89th percentile) with Brent at $105.66/bbl is a current account problem that a pause cannot solve.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — up from 75.6% — is the most credible signal of a genuine investment upcycle: historically, utilisation above 75% triggers fresh private capex commitments within two to three quarters. The contradiction is core sector at 5.4% YoY, down from 6.0%, which suggests infrastructure-linked capex is moderating even as manufacturing investment accelerates. GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month — a 14.8% month-on-month jump — corroborates broad economic activity, though the question is how much of that jump is genuine demand versus advance filing seasonality.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY signal that both urban and rural demand are holding — two-wheelers are the more reliable rural proxy, and 19.7% is not a weak number. GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month is the formalization signal: the question is whether this reflects genuine new demand or existing informal spend being reclassified into the GST net. The inversion: if fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY is compressing real rural incomes, two-wheeler sales strength may be inventory restocking by dealers rather than end-consumer pull — check retail vs wholesale dispatch data before calling this a clean beat.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (down from 82.5% prior month) remains elevated at 75th percentile historically. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% YoY prior) signals wholesale funding pressure. Industry credit surging at 20% YoY and services credit at 22.9% YoY — both concentrated in sectors with lower deposit bases.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% and deposit franchises in metros — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; liquidity stress will force asset sales or margin compression. RBI will likely ease liquidity via OMOs or CRR cuts within 2-3 months if deposit growth doesn't accelerate. Position for a 25-50 bps rate cut by Q3 FY27.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile has historically preceded either deposit acceleration or RBI policy easing. Last time CD ratio was this elevated (2022), RBI cut rates 250 bps over 12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals robust investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6% prior month) — at 74th percentile, a level that historically triggers fresh capex. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6% prior) shows some moderation but remains positive. GST collections at ₹199,853 cr / month (up from ₹174,116 cr / month prior) — a 14.8% month-on-month jump — indicate broad-based economic activity. India GDP FY estimate at 7.7% YoY (80th percentile) and RBI GDP forecast at 6.7% YoY (76th percentile) both revised upward.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Capex-linked sectors (construction equipment, industrial machinery) will see 12-18 month tailwinds. Public sector capex remains the anchor; private capex will follow as capacity utilisation sustains above 76%. Avoid defensive sectors — earnings growth will be driven by volume, not margin expansion. Allocate to companies with order books > 2 years of revenue.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at the 74th percentile and has historically preceded 18-24 months of capex acceleration. Last cycle (2014-2018), capex growth peaked 6-9 months after CU crossed 76%.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (up from ₹31,961 cr / month prior) — rising 2 consecutive months and at 92nd percentile. SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (up from ₹18.21 lakh cr prior) — at 93rd percentile and rising 2 consecutive months. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (up from 99.06 mn prior) — at 82nd percentile. However, SIP YoY growth at 14% (down from 16% prior) signals deceleration. MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (at 86th percentile) and average AUM at ₹88.31 lakh cr (at 88th percentile) both rising 2 consecutive months. DII equity net flows at ₹58,502 cr net / month (at 100th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months) — domestic institutions are the primary driver.","implication":"SIP account growth of 1.1% MoM is slowing, but AUM growth of 2.3% MoM indicates rising ticket sizes — affluent retail is entering, not mass retail. This is late-cycle behaviour. Rotate from small-cap SIP-driven rallies into large-cap quality and dividend payers. Expect SIP flows to remain sticky above ₹30,000 cr / month for next 6 months, but growth rate will decelerate. Overweight large-cap financials and IT — they have the highest SIP penetration.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile have historically preceded market corrections within 3-6 months as retail euphoria peaks. Last peak (Jan 2024) preceded a 12% correction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% YoY prior) — at 95th percentile, the highest in the dataset. WPI at 9.92% YoY (up from 9.78% prior) and rising. Brent crude at $105.66 / bbl (up 4 of last 5 months, from $103.4 / bbl low). WTI at $94.81 / bbl (up 4 of last 5 months). Natural gas at $3.28 / MMBtu (up 3 of last 5 months). CPI headline at 4.45% YoY (up from 4.38% prior) and core CPI at 3.9% YoY — both above RBI's 4% target. RBI inflation forecast revised up to 5.1% YoY (from 4.6% prior).","implication":"RBI will NOT cut rates in the next 2-3 months despite deposit stress. Repo rate will remain at 5.25% p.a. until fuel inflation moderates below 15% YoY. This creates a liquidity squeeze for NBFCs and smaller banks. Hedge long-duration bond positions — 10-year yields will remain sticky above 5.2%. Overweight energy stocks and underweight rate-sensitive sectors (auto, housing). India's CAD will widen if oil stays above $105 / bbl; expect INR depreciation pressure.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile has historically preceded 6-12 months of RBI rate pause. Last spike (2022) led to 12-month pause followed by 250 bps cuts.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"Fed Tightening Diverges from BOJ Easing","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (up from 3.63% prior, rising 2 in a row) — at 68th percentile. US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.21% (down from 5.24% prior) but at 94th percentile historically — a signal of terminal rate expectations. BOJ rate at 1% p.a. (up from 0.75% prior) — at 86th percentile, a strong-negative signal as BOJ tightens. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (up from 2% prior). US PMI composite at 56 index (up from 54.5 prior) — at 84th percentile. US GDP SAAR at 2.2% (up from 2.5% prior) but rising 2 consecutive months. US CPI at 3.72% YoY (up from 3.35% prior). DXY at 102.215 index (flat, at 56th percentile). US VIX at 16.87 index (flat, at 11th percentile — very low).","implication":"Carry trade unwind risk is rising as BOJ tightens while Fed pauses. DXY will likely move higher if Fed signals further tightening; this pressures INR and emerging market currencies. US 10-year yields at 94th percentile suggest limited upside; expect range-bound 5.0-5.3% for next 2-3 months. Reduce leverage in carry trades. Overweight USD-denominated assets and underweight INR-denominated bonds. Watch for BOJ policy divergence — if BOJ accelerates tightening, yen carry unwind could trigger 500+ bps INR depreciation in weeks.","pct_10y":68,"pct_note":"Fed funds at 68th percentile with BOJ at 86th percentile is a rare divergence. Last time (2015-2016), this preceded 18 months of EM currency weakness and carry trade volatility.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"watch","title":"INR Weakening as FII Flows Reverse","data_text":"INR at 95.24 ₹ / USD (flat from 95.29 prior, at 89th percentile — historically weak). FII equity net flows at ₹29,631 cr net / month (up from ₹20,200 cr prior) — at 83rd percentile but volatile (recent: -114 → -3,111.9 → +29,631). India VIX at 14.625 index (up from 14.12 prior, at 10th percentile — very low volatility). US 10-year Treasury at 5.21% yield (at 94th percentile) creates carry incentive for FIIs to rotate into US bonds. Brent at $105.66 / bbl (up 4 of last 5 months) will widen India's CAD. India household debt at 42.6% of GDP (at 51st percentile) and corporate debt at 51.9% of GDP (at 42nd percentile) — both moderate.","implication":"INR is vulnerable to 96.5-97.5 ₹ / USD if FII flows reverse or US yields spike above 5.3%. RBI will likely intervene to defend 96 ₹ / USD but has limited ammunition if oil stays elevated. Hedge INR exposure via forwards or options. Avoid INR-denominated bonds with duration > 5 years. Overweight exporters (IT, pharma, textiles) — they benefit from INR weakness. Watch FII flows closely; if they turn negative for 2 consecutive months, INR will break 96.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile (historically weak) has preceded 6-12 months of further depreciation. Last time (2022-2023), INR weakened from 75 to 83 over 12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Surge Masks Structural Vacancy Crisis","data_text":"Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter (up from 11.2 mn sq ft prior, at 7th percentile — historically very low) — rising 3 of last 5 quarters. However, office vacancy at 14.37% vacant (down from 14.45% prior, at 41st percentile) remains stubbornly elevated. Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (down from 5% prior, at 7th percentile) — a strong-positive signal (score: +86). Rent in Bengaluru at ₹103.6 / sqft / month (up from ₹96.3 prior) and Mumbai at ₹135.8 / sqft / month (up from ₹129.4 prior) — both rising. Real estate unsold inventory at 630,600 units (up 4 of last 5 months, at 65th percentile). Home loan disbursements at ₹19,930 cr / quarter (up from ₹15,914 cr prior, at 0th percentile — data is sparse). Affordability index at 10.9 × price ÷ income (down from 11.2 prior, at 100th percentile — worst affordability on record).","implication":"Office absorption is being driven by GCC (Global Capability Centers) and non-IT tenants, NOT traditional IT services. This decouples commercial RE from Nifty IT stock performance — IT stocks are flat while office rents rise. Retail mall vacancy collapse (4.8%) signals e-commerce saturation and return to physical retail — a structural shift. However, residential RE is in a affordability crisis (10.9x price-to-income is worst on record) despite rising home loan disbursements. This suggests only affluent buyers are entering; mass-market housing demand is stalling. Overweight commercial RE REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) and retail landlords — they will see 8-12% rent growth. Underweight residential developers with > 40% inventory in sub-₹50 lakh segment. The residential RE boom is ending; commercial RE is just beginning.","pct_10y":7,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 7th percentile is historically very low, but the composition has shifted from IT to GCCs and non-IT corporates. This is a structural change that equity analysts have missed — they still model office RE as an IT proxy. Retail mall vacancy at 7th percentile (best in cycle) signals e-commerce deceleration and omnichannel retail return.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Services Carry GDP While Goods Economy Quietly Moderates

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY — but IIP overall slowed to 6.7% YoY from 8.8% and core sector eased to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%, narrowing the base of growth.
  • PMI Composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is services-driven: PMI Services at 54.5 while PMI Manufacturing slips to 52.8.
  • Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile, up from 75.6%) is the one unambiguous positive — historically the threshold that triggers fresh private capex.
  • But GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month — a 14.8% month-on-month jump — may partly reflect advance filings rather than a clean demand surge.

The tension: The GDP headline and the PMI composite both look expansionary; the goods-economy proxies (IIP, core sector) are decelerating. Growth is real but narrowing to formal services — a segment that employs a fraction of the workforce.

Bottom line: Watch IIP capital goods sustaining above 12% YoY for two more months as the confirmation that the investment cycle is broad-based, not a single-quarter statistical artefact.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Equities at Peak Percentiles — Bond Market Disagrees

The facts:

  • Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,190 (100th percentile) and S&P 500 at 7,719 (100th percentile) — both at historic highs — while US GDP SAAR slowed to 2.2% SAAR from 2.5%.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.21% yield (94th percentile) is doing the Fed's tightening for it; real economy stress is embedded in the curve, not yet in equity prices.
  • BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) is the underappreciated tail: yen carry unwinds historically arrive with a 60–90 day lag after BOJ moves.
  • But China PMI Composite at 49.5 (contraction) and China GDP at 4.3% YoY (down from 5.0%) remove the commodity-reflation backstop that DM equity bulls are implicitly assuming.

The tension: DM equity markets are priced for a soft landing; the bond market at 5.21% yield and China's sub-50 PMI are priced for something less comfortable. One of them is wrong.

Bottom line: BOJ's next move is the underpriced risk for India liquidity — a further hike toward 1.25% p.a. would accelerate yen carry unwinds and pressure EM flows within 60–90 days.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Savings Flood In — But the Deposit Engine Is Stalling

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile, rising two consecutive months) and DII equity net flows at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile) are providing a structural bid under equities.
  • But SIP YoY growth decelerated to 14% YoY from 16% — the marginal retail saver is slowing even as the absolute level holds.
  • Bank deposit growth at 10.8% YoY against credit growth at 17.1% YoY — a 630bps gap — means the same household savings pool is being competed for by banks, MFs, and REITs simultaneously.
  • FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month (83rd percentile) looks positive but the recent sequence (-114 → -3,112 → +29,631) signals volatility, not conviction.

The tension: Domestic institutional flows are at record levels, masking the fragility: deposit growth is insufficient to fund credit growth, and SIP momentum is decelerating at the margin. The DII bid is real; its durability depends on retail income growth that fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY is quietly eroding.

Bottom line: Watch deposit growth — if it stays below 12% YoY while credit holds above 16% YoY, a macro-prudential response on risk weights becomes the base case within two quarters.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Demand Holds the Premium Segment — Affordability Locks Out Everyone Else

The facts:

  • NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 10 percentage points vs prior period), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25% — remittances at $73 bn (12.8% YoY) are the funding source; Mumbai Metropolitan Region and Bengaluru are the primary destinations.
  • Affordability index at 10.9× price ÷ income — the worst reading in the 10-year dataset — with average home loan rates at 7.65% p.a. means domestic mass-market buyers are effectively priced out.
  • Unsold inventory at 630,600 units (up four of last five months) while Hyderabad launches surged 120% YoY — supply is being added into a market where only the top two ticket-size bands are clearing.
  • Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter (7th percentile historically) with vacancy still at 14.37% vacant — GCCs (41% of occupier mix) and BFSI (22%) are absorbing space; IT services at 15% is not.
  • But REIT prices tell the real story: Embassy at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit — all down sharply from prior prints, pricing the vacancy overhang the absorption headline obscures.

The tension: NRI and affluent domestic capital is sustaining the premium segment; the mass market is frozen by record-low affordability. Office absorption looks healthy in aggregate but vacancy refuses to clear — the GCC and BFSI demand is real, but it is not enough to absorb the legacy IT-services overhang.

Bottom line: Avoid broad residential developer exposure; the NRI-premium thesis is intact for Mumbai and Bengaluru luxury, but unsold inventory at 630,600 units rising for four consecutive months is a supply trap for mid-segment developers.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Crude Is the Common Thread

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $105.66/bbl rising four of last five months — every $10/bbl adds ~$15 bn to India's import bill, widening CAD by ~40bps and pressuring INR at an already-weak 89th percentile.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) with credit growing at 17.1% YoY vs deposits at 10.8% YoY — NBFC credit at 14.9% YoY signals wholesale funding stress is building.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile) — a further hike would accelerate yen carry unwinds; India's FII equity flows at ₹29,631 cr net / month are volatile enough that a reversal would test DII absorption capacity.
  • Affordability index at 10.9× price ÷ income (100th percentile worst) with home loan rates at 7.65% p.a. — any further rate rise or INR depreciation feeding into imported construction costs could freeze residential transaction volumes.

The tension: Crude is the single variable that simultaneously worsens inflation, widens CAD, pressures INR, delays rate cuts, and erodes real household income — four of the five risks above have Brent as a common input.

Bottom line: Watch Brent at the $108/bbl threshold — a sustained break above that level forces RBI to choose between defending INR and protecting growth, and the policy pause becomes untenable.

"}
